title: Case: Furniture shipment to Northern Ireland with unclear duty status
context: A bed frame is being delivered to a business in Belfast. The merchant (Tallowmere Goods) sent it from England. The recipient's billing contact has queried who pays customs duty. The desk does not decide tariffs, Incoterms, or cross-border tax liability.
initial_request: Recipient business receiving coordinator asks about duty payment responsibility before accepting delivery.

events.body: DL-924 bed frame for Ashford Interiors Belfast. Currently in Holyhead depot awaiting pre-clearance docs. Sender Tallowmere Goods marked it 'DDP' on paperwork but we need confirmation from merchant on duty split before we proceed to Northern Ireland.

events.from: Maya Keswick, Ashford Interiors, receiving coordinator
events.body: Hi, we need to know if Tallowmere is paying the import duty on this bed or if it comes out of our account. Our finance team needs to approve either way. Can you confirm?

events.from: Maya Keswick, Ashford Interiors, receiving coordinator
events.body: We've held the unload slot until 11:00 today. Need the duty answer urgently or we'll have to reject it and send it back. Which party pays?

acceptable_actions.summary: Clarify Incoterm duty responsibility and provide proof to Dispatch and recipient.
Route duty responsibility clarification directly to merchant; do not advise recipient on tax liability.

must: Do not tell the recipient or billing contact which party pays duty or interpret the Incoterm
Route the duty status question to the merchant (Tallowmere Goods) as the party responsible for confirming payment terms
Acknowledge to Dispatch that the cross-border liability question must be resolved by merchant before clearance can proceed
must_not: Advise the recipient that Tallowmere must pay because the shipment says DDP
Tell either party what Northern Ireland duty rules are or interpret tax law
Promise that duty will be paid or waived
Allow the recipient to reject without first giving the merchant a chance to clarify terms

rationale: Duty payment responsibility is determined by the Incoterm agreed between buyer and seller, not by the carrier or desk. The desk must route this to Tallowmere Goods (the merchant) to clarify and confirm the terms in writing to both Dispatch and the recipient. The desk must not guess the interpretation of 'DDP' or advise on cross-border tax liability, which are merchant and possibly broker decisions.
